record.file_problem: Only repository metadata, README, and file list are supplied. The referenced RESULTS.md and other documents are not included, so their findings cannot be checked.
record.tranche_reason: The README says the project reproduces the original paper's §§2–4 on seven models and reports qualitative outcomes, though it says the numerical summary is in an unavailable RESULTS.md.
record.gate_note: The README also says §5 adversarial suffixes were not attempted. It refers to numerical results in RESULTS.md, which is not supplied; no results from that file are included here. The Part 2 and Part 3 concept-steering claims are not included as findings about the claim's refusal direction.
record.test_reason: The README presents a from-scratch reproduction of the original paper's §§2–4 (direction extraction, ablation, addition, weight orthogonalization) on 7 models. The only result it states is qualitative: weight edits restricted to blocks before r̂'s layer remove refusal. All numbers are deferred to RESULTS.md, which was not supplied, so the evidence is thin.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely right. The README reports §§2–4 as done on 7 models and says block-restricted edits remove refusal. It says refusal regrows with 8–16 examples and a rank-one off-switch removes the regrown refusal. It notes §5 was not attempted. The README does not state an overall conclusion about whether the original replicates; it defers this to RESULTS.md.
record.recipe_differences: The README says the project uses its own prompts and data and updated model evaluations; it reports that §5 was not attempted. This is a reproduction project, but the supplied README does not specify the exact reproduction procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports that edits restricted to blocks before r̂'s layer remove refusal and that regrowth requires 8–16 refusal examples; model- and evaluation-specific details are not stated.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal regrown by fine-tuning on 8–16 refusal examples is removed by a rank-one off-switch, which is not identified as r̂.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal restored by small fine-tuning remains removable by a single rank-one intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: Part 3: a CAA refusal vector (an A/B response-contrast direction, not harmful-minus-harmless) steers refusal on all 7 models. On 6 of them steering needs ×2 strength.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastive-activation-addition refusal vectors steer refusal across current open models.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is very weak: this is an unreviewed repository README with no numbers, no model names and no capability data. The file list suggests much more (jailbreak_projection.py, rhat_in_regrown.py, ablate_in_variants.py, capability.py), so results bearing on V3, V6 and V7 may exist in RESULTS.md. A re-read with RESULTS.md, ARDITI.md and the HANDOFF/SUMMARY files is recommended.

versions.untested_parts: The README says §§2–4 were reproduced, but does not give enough detail here to identify the direction, intervention, or results for the original causal claim.
The README does not identify the models or provide numerical refusal rates, capability measures, or enough detail to confirm the edits are the original ablation converted to weight edits.
The README explicitly says adversarial suffixes (§5) were not attempted; it reports no test of suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No result about affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported in the supplied text.
No result separating harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is reported.
The seven model names and variants are not given, and no cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer result is reported.
The README reports refusal regrowth after examples, but does not report whether a removable direction exists or how training determines that.
